precepts.text: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel. Voodoo and roots are enchantment; it does not work on us. But step outside the zone and use it yourself and you will be bugged out of your mind, clucking like a chicken. Zodiac signs are divination too; we are not supposed to be in the midst of that; it is against the commandments of the Most High.
precepts.point: Video played from Haiti: Bishop Canaan holding up a speaker with Bishop Nathanyel teaching in the midst, surrounded on all corners, hot, no place to hold post; it was raining so we relocated under a shelter and did not stop the work. We walked down five, six, seven flights of stairs into the mountains, deep down into the middle of a voodoo festival, surrounded, teaching morality, because what the wicked stumble at is the moral law and the ceremonial law, idolatry, vexing the Most High to his face. In the valley, teaching our people to return, repent, come back to the one true God and the Bible; why are you in the midst of darkness? Those are the ones with the mark, who sigh and cry. They even took our flyers and stuck them in the stumps of the trees to try to put something on us. It does not work; we understand the scriptures.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

precepts.why:
The mark is set “upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.” In Haiti the men of the Lord walked down five, six, seven flights of stairs, deep into the mountains, into the middle of a voodoo festival, surrounded on all corners, teaching our people to return, repent and come back to the one true God and the Bible. Why are you in the midst of darkness? While we taught, they took our flyers and stuck them in the stumps of the trees, trying to put something on us.

It does not work. “Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!” Voodoo is enchantment. Roots is another word for it; that is enchantment too. That is what the Bible says about it: it does not work on us.

But go ahead and step outside of the zone and use it yourself. You are going to get bugged out of your mind, clucking like a chicken, seeing invisible wheelbarrows going on down the mountain. You are finished. That is what happens.

And a lot of people are into the zodiac signs. That is divination. We are not supposed to be in the midst of that; it is against the commandments of the Most High. The servants who sigh and cry go right into the midst of that darkness unafraid, because we understand the scriptures, and no enchantment or divination can touch Israel.

precepts.text: The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea; that is the dust of Jacob no man can count.
precepts.point: Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his. The last end of Israel is a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord: the land married, double for our shame, everlasting joy, and a seed acknowledged among the Gentiles as the seed which the Lord hath blessed. That is why we cannot wait for those days.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
“Who can count the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel?” No man can. “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

Israel is as the sand of the sea; that is the dust of Jacob no man can count. And Hosea says where it ends: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The people that shall dwell alone and not be reckoned among the nations are the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: Israel's last end is a crown of glory and a royal diadem, the land no more termed forsaken but married, and the Most High rejoicing over her as a bridegroom over the bride.
precepts.point: Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his. The last end of Israel is a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord: the land married, double for our shame, everlasting joy, and a seed acknowledged among the Gentiles as the seed which the Lord hath blessed. That is why we cannot wait for those days.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
“Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his!” What is the last end of Israel? “Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.”

“Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzi–bah, and thy land Beulah: for the Lord delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.” The land no more termed forsaken but married, and the Most High rejoicing over her: “as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.”

That is the last end Balaam wished for himself, a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and it is why we cannot wait for those days.

precepts.text: For your shame ye shall have double, an everlasting covenant, and a seed known among the Gentiles as the seed which the Lord hath blessed.
precepts.point: Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his. The last end of Israel is a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord: the land married, double for our shame, everlasting joy, and a seed acknowledged among the Gentiles as the seed which the Lord hath blessed. That is why we cannot wait for those days.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
The last end of Israel that Balaam wished to share: “For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.” Double for our shame, and everlasting joy.

“For I the Lord love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.” An everlasting covenant, and a seed the nations will know: “And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.”

The people that shall not be reckoned among the nations will be acknowledged by all that see them as the seed which the Lord hath blessed. That is why we cannot wait for those days.

precepts.text: Go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them.
precepts.point: The house of Israel is impudent and hardhearted, so the Lord makes the face and forehead strong, meaning the mind: whatever excuse the people raise, He gives an answer through the scriptures on the spot. The rebellious spirits on our people are only cast down by the word of God, which is why we speak what the Lord puts in our mouth.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
Balak charged Balaam with blessing his enemies altogether, and Balaam answered, “Must I not take heed to speak that which the Lord hath put in my mouth?” That is the same charge given to Ezekiel.

“And he said unto me, Son of man, go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them.” It is what every man must do who speaks on behalf of the Most High, especially the brothers: go unto the house of Israel and speak with His words unto them, not our own.

precepts.text: The house of Israel is impudent and hardhearted, but the Lord makes thy face strong against their faces; fear them not, though they be a rebellious house.
precepts.point: The house of Israel is impudent and hardhearted, so the Lord makes the face and forehead strong, meaning the mind: whatever excuse the people raise, He gives an answer through the scriptures on the spot. The rebellious spirits on our people are only cast down by the word of God, which is why we speak what the Lord puts in our mouth.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
Balaam had to take heed to speak what the Lord put in his mouth, and the man sent to Israel must do the same, because of who he is sent to. “But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee; for they will not hearken unto me: for all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted.”

So the Lord makes the face and forehead strong, meaning the mind: “Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads. As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they be a rebellious house.” Whatever excuse the people raise, He gives an answer through the scriptures on the spot.

The rebellious spirits on our people are only cast down by the word of God, which is why we speak what the Lord puts in our mouth, as Balaam had to.

precepts.text: Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed; once judgment is passed there is no crossing it, because God is not a man that he should lie.
precepts.point: That is what we doubted back in Deuteronomy when Moses read the curses over us; we thought the Lord would not make good on His word. But the Lord is longsuffering and patient and will in no wise acquit the wicked; we will not escape our sins.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
“God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent.” Whatever the Lord speaks out of His mouth, once the judgment is passed there is no taking it back, whether in this life or the one to come. The parable of Lazarus shows it.

“But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.”

The judgment has been set and there is no changing it. A great gulf fixed, so that none can pass, because God is not a man that He should lie: hath He said, and shall He not do it?

precepts.text: In the day of doom no man shall be able to save him that is destroyed; the sentence stands for ever.
precepts.point: That is what we doubted back in Deuteronomy when Moses read the curses over us; we thought the Lord would not make good on His word. But the Lord is longsuffering and patient and will in no wise acquit the wicked; we will not escape our sins.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
Hath He spoken, and shall He not make it good? Esdras tried asking the Most High to spare the wicked for the prayers of the righteous, and was told to concern himself with the righteous. “This present life is not the end where much glory doth abide; therefore have they prayed for the weak.”

“But the day of doom shall be the end of this time, and the beginning of the immortality for to come, wherein corruption is past, Intemperance is at an end, infidelity is cut off, righteousness is grown, and truth is sprung up. Then shall no man be able to save him that is destroyed, nor to oppress him that hath gotten the victory.” In the day of doom no man shall be able to save him that is destroyed; the sentence stands for ever.

This present life is not the end, and asking the righteous to pray for those that outright despise God and His laws is praying for the weak. That is what we doubted back in Deuteronomy when Moses read the curses over us; we thought the Lord would not make good on His word. But the Lord is longsuffering and patient and will in no wise acquit the wicked; we will not escape our sins.

precepts.text: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it?
precepts.point: And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent. The Strength of Israel is the Most High. Understand the spirit of the title: whenever you go off on your own mind, pride has you departing from your strength, and once you have left your strength you are open to Satan; if a brother tells you that you are battling with pride, take heed and examine yourself.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
As Samuel turned about to go away, Saul “laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle, and it rent.” Samuel said, “The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.” Just as Saul tore the hem of the garment, so the Lord tore the throne from him. Samuel says this still before he has ever met David, the same word he gave in chapter 13.

“And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent.” “God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?” What he said over Saul, he will do.

The Strength of Israel is the Most High. Understand the spirit of the title: whenever you go off on your own mind, pride has you departing from your strength, and once you have left your strength you are open to Satan. If a brother tells you that you are battling with pride, take heed and examine yourself.

precepts.text: God is not a man that he should lie; hath he said, and shall he not do it? This is why the testimony is so sure, because he will perform his word.
precepts.point: The testimony of the Lord is sure; the testimonies and prophecies in this Bible are sure.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
Why is the testimony so sure? “God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?”

God is not a man that he should lie. Whatever he has said, he will do it; whatever he has spoken, he will make it good. That is why the testimony of the Lord is sure: he will perform his word.

points: Sacrificing animals was not solely a thing pertaining to Israel; sacrificing for sin is what pertained to Israel. All the ancient nations of old sacrificed animals when they worshipped their gods, so Balak and Balaam offering bullocks and rams on altars was nothing new to them.
Offering animals on altars had been done since the time of Adam. It was commonplace in that time, so do not be confused at why Balaam keeps calling for altars and offerings through this chapter.

points: Balak the king of Moab brought Balaam from Aram to curse Jacob and defy Israel, and Balaam could not do it: how shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed?

points: God brought them out of Egypt; he hath as it were the strength of an unicorn. The unicorn in biblical times is the rhinoceros, the beast with the one great horn on the front.
